verses.text: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron, and spoke, saying, “Behold, we are your bone and your flesh.
In times past, when Saul was king over us, it was you who led Israel out and in. Yahweh said to you, ‘You will be shepherd of my people Israel, and you will be prince over Israel.’”
So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron, and king David made a covenant with them in Hebron before Yahweh; and they anointed David king over Israel.
David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months; and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.

The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, who spoke to David, saying, “The blind and the lame will keep you out of here”; thinking, “David can’t come in here.”
Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion. This is David’s city.

David said on that day, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites, let him go up to the watercourse and strike the lame and the blind, who are hated by David’s soul.” Therefore they say, “The blind and the lame can’t come into the house.”
David lived in the stronghold, and called it David’s city. David built around from Millo and inward.
David grew greater and greater; for Yahweh, the God of Armies, was with him.
Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar trees, carpenters, and masons; and they built David a house.
David perceived that Yahweh had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel’s sake.
David took more concubines and wives for himself out of Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron; and more sons and daughters were born to David.
These are the names of those who were born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
When the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David, but David heard about it and went down to the stronghold.
Now the Philistines had come and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.

David inquired of Yahweh, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver them into my hand?” Yahweh said to David, “Go up; for I will certainly deliver the Philistines into your hand.”
David came to Baal Perazim, and David struck them there. Then he said, “Yahweh has broken my enemies before me, like the breach of waters.” Therefore he called the name of that place Baal Perazim.
They left their images there; and David and his men took them away.
The Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
When David inquired of Yahweh, he said, “You shall not go up. Circle around behind them, and attack them in front of the mulberry trees.
When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, then stir yourself up; for then Yahweh has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”
David did so, as Yahweh commanded him, and struck the Philistines all the way from Geba to Gezer.

footnotes.content: All Israel comes to David, claiming kinship—'bone and flesh.' There's something tender here: they see themselves in him. After years apart, a people remember their shepherd and come home to him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this chapter's pattern: the Lord doesn't force His way in; He works through the hearts of people who remember and consent. We still recognize His shepherding, still invite Him in, still find victory comes when we ask and obey. The stronghold is still His.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They recall what David did when Saul ruled: he *led them out and in*—a shepherd's work, not a king's pride. And Yahweh had promised it. Sometimes the Lord prepares us long before the people see it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A covenant in Hebron before Yahweh, sealed by anointing. This isn't conquest—it's consent, made sacred. The Lord works through the hearts of His people, not around them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Thirty when he began to reign, forty years total—a long reign. The Lord didn't rush him into kingship, and didn't cut it short. There's a pace to faithful work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven and a half years in Hebron over Judah; thirty-three in Jerusalem ruling all. The move to the capital is the moment the kingdom consolidates. Patience, then boldness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Jebusites mock David: 'The blind and lame will stop you'—mocking his very ability to enter. Fear and contempt often wear the same face; both are a kind of lie.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He takes Zion, the stronghold, and it becomes David's city. A place once thought impregnable becomes a home. The Lord opens what we thought was locked.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David's words here are cryptic but decisive—he despises those who oppose him. The city itself becomes a boundary: inside is the people of the Lord; outside, defiance. Grace draws lines.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He lives in the stronghold, calls it David's city, builds outward from Millo. A king makes a place his home, not his trophy. He stays, he tends, he grows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David grew greater and greater—not by his strength, but by Yahweh's presence. 'The God of Armies was with him.' All honor belongs to Him alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hiram sends cedar, craftsmen, builders—worldly kings recognize the Lord's favor on David. When we walk close to Him, even strangers see it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David *perceived* that Yahweh had established him. He didn't assume it; he saw it and understood: the kingdom isn't his achievement but the Lord's gift, exalted for Israel's sake.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He took concubines and wives in Jerusalem after Hebron—many sons and daughters followed. Power and prosperity brought him a household, but the text doesn't hide the darkness ahead.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Names of David's children in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet. Among these, Nathan and Solomon point to the line that brings Jesus. The Lord works through families.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Philistines heard David was king and rose up to crush him. But he heard and went down to the stronghold—he didn't panic, he positioned himself. Wisdom and courage walk together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Philistines spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim, a place-name that speaks of ancient giants. History and memory gather in a single valley.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David asks Yahweh plainly: 'Shall I go up? Will you deliver them?' And the answer is clear and bold: 'Go up; I will deliver them.' He doesn't move without asking; he doesn't doubt after he's asked.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At Baal Perazim—'Lord of the Breach'—David strikes them, and names the place by what happened: 'Yahweh has broken my enemies before me, like the breach of waters.' A place-name that remembers God's power.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Philistines left their idols; David and his men took them away. A victory includes clearing out what was false. No space for both the Lord and hollow gods.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They came up again, spread themselves again in Rephaim. Defeat doesn't always teach foes to stop trying. But the faithful know: this battle is not theirs to settle once.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This time, Yahweh says: 'Don't go up direct. Circle around; attack from the front of the mulberry trees.' The second battle takes a different shape. Obedience sometimes means doing what didn't work last time—in a new way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Listen for the sound of marching in the mulberry tops—that's the sign to stir yourself, for Yahweh has gone out before you. The Lord moves first; we follow the sound of His presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David did as Yahweh commanded, struck the Philistines all the way from Geba to Gezer—a complete rout. When we follow the Lord's word exactly, the victory is complete.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
